GHSA-rfqq-wq6w-72jm.title: MLflow has a Local File Read/Path Traversal bypass
GHSA-rfqq-wq6w-72jm.text: MLflow has a Local File Read/Path Traversal bypass Affected: mlflow. Severity: HIGH. from 2.9.2; fixed in 2.12.1 A path traversal vulnerability exists in mlflow/mlflow version 2.11.0, identified as a bypass for the previously addressed CVE-2023-6909. The vulnerability arises from the application's handling of artifact URLs, where a '#' character can be used to insert a path into the fragment, effectively skipping validation. This allows an attacker to construct a URL that, when processed, ignores the protocol scheme and uses the provided path for filesystem access. As a result, an attacker can read arbitrary files, including sensitive information such as SSH and cloud keys, by exploiting the way the application converts the URL into a filesystem path. The issue stems from insufficient validation of the fragment portion of the URL, leading to arbitrary file read through path traversal.

GHSA-hq88-wg7q-gp4g.title: mlflow vulnerable to Path Traversal
GHSA-hq88-wg7q-gp4g.text: mlflow vulnerable to Path Traversal Affected: mlflow. Severity: CRITICAL. from 0; fixed in 2.10.0 mlflow/mlflow is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion (LFI) due to improper parsing of URIs, allowing attackers to bypass checks and read arbitrary files on the system. The issue arises from the 'is_local_uri' function's failure to properly handle URIs with empty or 'file' schemes, leading to the misclassification of URIs as non-local. Attackers can exploit this by crafting malicious model versions with specially crafted 'source' parameters, enabling the reading of sensitive files within at least two directory levels from the server's root.

GHSA-5q6c-ffvg-xcm9.title: Remote code execution in mlflow
GHSA-5q6c-ffvg-xcm9.text: Remote code execution in mlflow Affected: mlflow. Severity: CRITICAL. from 0; fixed in 2.9.0 A vulnerability in mlflow/mlflow version 8.2.1 allows for remote code execution due to improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command ('Command Injection') within the `mlflow.data.http_dataset_source.py` module. Specifically, when loading a dataset from a source URL with an HTTP scheme, the filename extracted from the `Content-Disposition` header or the URL path is used to generate the final file path without proper sanitization. This flaw enables an attacker to control the file path fully by utilizing path traversal or absolute path techniques, such as '../../tmp/poc.txt' or '/tmp/poc.txt', leading to arbitrary file write. Exploiting this vulnerability could allow a malicious user to execute commands on the vulnerable machine, potentially gaining access to data and model information. The issue is fixed in version 2.9.0.

GHSA-8f8q-q2j7-7j2m.text: Undefined Behavior in mlflow Affected: mlflow. Severity: MODERATE. from 0; fixed in 2.11.3 A vulnerability in mlflow/mlflow version 2.11.1 allows attackers to create multiple models with the same name by exploiting URL encoding. This flaw can lead to Denial of Service (DoS) as an authenticated user might not be able to use the intended model, as it will open a different model each time. Additionally, an attacker can exploit this vulnerability to perform data model poisoning by creating a model with the same name, potentially causing an authenticated user to become a victim by using the poisoned model. The issue stems from inadequate validation of model names, allowing for the creation of models with URL-encoded names that are treated as distinct from their URL-decoded counterparts.

PYSEC-2024-51.title: PYSEC-2024-51
PYSEC-2024-51.text: PYSEC-2024-51 Affected: mlflow. Severity: unrated. from 0; fixed in b43e0e3de5b500554e13dc032ba2083b2d6c94b8; from 0; fixed in 2.10.1 A broken access control vulnerability exists in mlflow/mlflow versions before 2.10.1, where low privilege users with only EDIT permissions on an experiment can delete any artifacts. This issue arises due to the lack of proper validation for DELETE requests by users with EDIT permissions, allowing them to perform unauthorized deletions of artifacts. The vulnerability specifically affects the handling of artifact deletions within the application, as demonstrated by the ability of a low privilege user to delete a directory inside an artifact using a DELETE request, despite the official documentation stating that users with EDIT permission can only read and update artifacts, not delete them.

GHSA-5mvj-wmgj-7q8c.title: mlflow vulnerable to Path Traversal
GHSA-5mvj-wmgj-7q8c.text: mlflow vulnerable to Path Traversal Affected: mlflow. Severity: HIGH. from 0 A path traversal vulnerability exists in the mlflow/mlflow repository, specifically within the artifact deletion functionality. Attackers can bypass path validation by exploiting the double decoding process in the `_delete_artifact_mlflow_artifacts` handler and `local_file_uri_to_path` function, allowing for the deletion of arbitrary directories on the server's filesystem. This vulnerability is due to an extra unquote operation in the `delete_artifacts` function of `local_artifact_repo.py`, which fails to properly sanitize user-supplied paths. The issue is present up to version 2.9.2, despite attempts to fix a similar issue in CVE-2023-6831.

GHSA-j46q-5pxx-8vmw.title: Local File Inclusion in mlflow
GHSA-j46q-5pxx-8vmw.text: Local File Inclusion in mlflow Affected: mlflow. Severity: HIGH. from 0; fixed in 2.11.3 A Local File Inclusion (LFI) vulnerability was identified in mlflow/mlflow, specifically in version 2.9.2, which was fixed in version 2.11.3. This vulnerability arises from the application's failure to properly validate URI fragments for directory traversal sequences such as '../'. An attacker can exploit this flaw by manipulating the fragment part of the URI to read arbitrary files on the local file system, including sensitive files like '/etc/passwd'. The vulnerability is a bypass to a previous patch that only addressed similar manipulation within the URI's query string, highlighting the need for comprehensive validation of all parts of a URI to prevent LFI attacks.

GHSA-j62r-wxqq-f3gf.title: mlflow vulnerable to Path Traversal
GHSA-j62r-wxqq-f3gf.text: mlflow vulnerable to Path Traversal Affected: mlflow. Severity: HIGH. from 0; fixed in 2.12.1 A path traversal vulnerability exists in the `_create_model_version()` function within `server/handlers.py` of the mlflow/mlflow repository, due to improper validation of the `source` parameter. Attackers can exploit this vulnerability by crafting a `source` parameter that bypasses the `_validate_non_local_source_contains_relative_paths(source)` function's checks, allowing for arbitrary file read access on the server. The issue arises from the handling of unquoted URL characters and the subsequent misuse of the original `source` value for model version creation, leading to the exposure of sensitive files when interacting with the `/model-versions/get-artifact` handler.

PYSEC-2024-224.text: PYSEC-2024-224 Affected: mlflow. Severity: unrated. from 0; fixed in 2.16.0 Excessive directory permissions in MLflow leads to local privilege escalation when using spark_udf. GHSA-p4jx-q62p-x5jr.title: MLflow allows low privilege users to delete any artifact
GHSA-p4jx-q62p-x5jr.text: MLflow allows low privilege users to delete any artifact Affected: mlflow. Severity: MODERATE. from 0; fixed in 2.10.1 A broken access control vulnerability exists in mlflow/mlflow versions before 2.10.1, where low privilege users with only EDIT permissions on an experiment can delete any artifacts. This issue arises due to the lack of proper validation for DELETE requests by users with EDIT permissions, allowing them to perform unauthorized deletions of artifacts. The vulnerability specifically affects the handling of artifact deletions within the application, as demonstrated by the ability of a low privilege user to delete a directory inside an artifact using a DELETE request, despite the official documentation stating that users with EDIT permission can only read and update artifacts, not delete them.

GHSA-wf7f-8fxf-xfxc.title: MLFlow unsafe deserialization

Severity: HIGH. from 0.5.0 Deserialization of untrusted data can occur in versions of the MLflow platform running version 0.5.0 or newer, enabling a maliciously uploaded PyTorch model to run arbitrary code on an end user’s system when interacted with.

PYSEC-2024-239.title: PYSEC-2024-239
PYSEC-2024-239.text: PYSEC-2024-239 Affected: mlflow. Severity: unrated. from 0; fixed in 400c226953b4568f4361bc0a0c223511652c2b9d; fixed in 400c226953b4568f4361bc0a0c223511652c2b9d; from 0; fixed in 2.9.0 A vulnerability in mlflow/mlflow version 8.2.1 allows for remote code execution due to improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command ('Command Injection') within the `mlflow.data.http_dataset_source.py` module. Specifically, when loading a dataset from a source URL with an HTTP scheme, the filename extracted from the `Content-Disposition` header or the URL path is used to generate the final file path without proper sanitization. This flaw enables an attacker to control the file path fully by utilizing path traversal or absolute path techniques, such as '../../tmp/poc.txt' or '/tmp/poc.txt', leading to arbitrary file write. Exploiting this vulnerability could allow a malicious user to execute commands on the vulnerable machine, potentially gaining access to data and model information. The issue is fixed in version 2.9.0.

PYSEC-2024-244.title: PYSEC-2024-244
PYSEC-2024-244.text: PYSEC-2024-244 Affected: mlflow. Severity: unrated. from 0; fixed in f8d51e21523238280ebcfdb378612afd7844eca8; fixed in f8d51e21523238280ebcfdb378612afd7844eca8; from 0; fixed in 2.12.1 A path traversal vulnerability exists in mlflow/mlflow version 2.11.0, identified as a bypass for the previously addressed CVE-2023-6909. The vulnerability arises from the application's handling of artifact URLs, where a '#' character can be used to insert a path into the fragment, effectively skipping validation. This allows an attacker to construct a URL that, when processed, ignores the protocol scheme and uses the provided path for filesystem access. As a result, an attacker can read arbitrary files, including sensitive information such as SSH and cloud keys, by exploiting the way the application converts the URL into a filesystem path. The issue stems from insufficient validation of the fragment portion of the URL, leading to arbitrary file read through path traversal.

GHSA-49m6-vrr9-2cqm.text: MLflow Uncontrolled Resource Consumption vulnerability Affected: mlflow. This can tie up all the workers allocated by MLFlow, rendering the application unable to respond to other requests. This vulnerability is due to uncontrolled resource consumption.

GHSA-4rqf-8pfm-p36r.text: MLflow has a Local File Read/Path Traversal in dbfs Affected: mlflow. This issue occurs because only the path part of the URL is checked, while parts such as query and parameters are not handled. The vulnerability is triggered if the user has configured the dbfs service, and during usage, the service is mounted to a local directory.
